subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by making CLI health/status/stability RPC-first with read-only/no-maintenance fallback, by adding a stricter single-writer gateway lease for all non-gateway state DB access, or by doing both?
rationale: Source confirms mutable/checkpointing shared-state open paths remain, but the durable fix changes product ownership between gateway observability, doctor migrations, plugin-state diagnostics, and operator recovery.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

options.title: Add a single-writer gateway lease
options.body: The gateway should own write and WAL maintenance access to the shared state DB, with non-gateway processes failing closed or using gateway APIs unless an explicit maintenance mode is active.

options.title: Forensics before direction
options.body: Pause code changes until the reporter's corrupt DB bundle and a native runtime harness prove the exact OpenClaw SQLite interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance fallback
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should be read-only with no journal or checkpoint pragmas.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture introduced in PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78595 and the current gateway/CLI ownership boundary.
